name: git-github-mcp
description: FastMCP 3.1+ portmanteau server: git_core/branch/admin/blame (43 local git ops) + github_ops (58 GitHub actions via gh CLI), two sampling agentic workflows, 7 prompts, optional FastAPI web bridge on port 10702.

tools.name: git_core
tools.description: Local Git core ops — status, log, diff, show, init, clone, add, commit, push, pull, fetch (11 ops)

tools.name: git_branch
tools.description: Git branch ops — branch lifecycle, merge, rebase, stash, tag (14 ops)

tools.name: git_admin
tools.description: Git admin ops — remote, reset, revert, cherry-pick, clean, submodule, bisect, worktree (16 ops)

tools.name: git_blame
tools.description: Git blame — annotate file lines with commit info

tools.name: github_ops
tools.description: GitHub via gh CLI — 58 actions: repos, issues, PRs, releases, Actions workflows, labels, secrets, collaborators, search, Projects, Packages, Gitingest, auth_status, gist_list

tools.name: git_github_status
tools.description: System status: git and gh CLI availability, versions, auth state

tools.name: git_github_help
tools.description: Contextual help for operations (level: basic/intermediate/advanced; topic: git_ops|github_ops)

tools.name: git_agentic_workflow
tools.description: Sampling: plan and execute multi-step git_core + github_ops from natural language (requires MCP sampling)

tools.name: git_github_search_workflow
tools.description: Sampling: GitHub discovery/search only — planned github_ops chain (requires MCP sampling)

prompts.name: git_commit_message
prompts.description: Generate a conventional commit message from a staged diff
prompts.text:
Write a conventional commit message for the following staged diff.

Rules:
- Format: <type>(<scope>): <short description>
- Types: feat, fix, docs, style, refactor, test, chore, ci, perf
- Subject line max 72 chars, imperative mood
- Add body if changes are non-trivial
- Add BREAKING CHANGE footer if applicable

Diff:
```
{{diff}}
```

Context: {{context}}

prompts.name: git_release_notes
prompts.description: Generate release notes from a commit log
prompts.text:
Write release notes for version {{version}}.

Format:
## What's Changed
Group commits into: Features, Bug Fixes, Documentation, Internal.
Skip trivial commits (chore: bump, style: format).

Commits:
```
{{commits}}
```

Repo: {{repo}}

prompts.name: git_pr_description
prompts.description: Generate a pull request description from branch and commits
prompts.text:
Write a pull request description for branch `{{branch}}`.

Include:
- ## Summary (what and why)
- ## Changes (bullet list)
- ## Testing (how to verify)
- ## Notes (breaking changes, migration steps, TODOs)

Commits:
```
{{commits}}
```

Changed files:
```
{{diff_stat}}
```

prompts.name: git_review_diff
prompts.description: Code review prompt for a git diff
prompts.text:
Review the following code diff.

Focus: {{focus}}

For each issue found:
- File and line reference
- Severity: critical / major / minor / nit
- Explanation and suggested fix

Also note what's done well.

Diff:
```
{{diff}}
```

prompts.name: github_issue_template
prompts.description: Generate a GitHub issue body (types: bug, feature, docs, question)
prompts.text:
Write a GitHub issue body for a {{type}} report.

Title: {{title}}
Context: {{context}}

For bug: Sections: Description, Steps to Reproduce, Expected Behavior, Actual Behavior, Environment.
For feature: Sections: Problem Statement, Proposed Solution, Alternatives Considered.
For docs: Sections: Current Documentation, What's Missing, Suggested Content.
For question: Sections: Question, What I've Tried, Relevant Code.

prompts.name: github_debug_workflow
prompts.description: Debug a failing GitHub Actions workflow from error output

prompts.name: git_github_explain_concept
prompts.description: Teach a Git/GitHub concept with examples (e.g. gitingest, agentic-workflows)
prompts.text:
Teach the concept '{{concept}}' at level '{{level}}'.

Output structure:
1. What it is (1-2 sentences)
2. When to use it / when not to use it
3. 2-4 practical commands/examples
4. Common failure modes and recovery commands
5. One short checklist the user can follow

Keep the explanation practical and non-fluffy.
